description: ``write_guard._is_protected`` and ``_is_allowed`` (plus ``plan_guard._is_exempt``) used ASCII-only ``.lower()`` to case-fold paths against PROTECTED_*/ALLOWED_*/EXEMPT_* prefix lists. Unicode-equivalent codepoints — fullwidth Latin (U+FF21..U+FF5A), Turkish dotted I (U+0130), German ß (U+00DF), and other compatibility variants — fold to the ASCII form on case-insensitive APFS via the filesystem's Unicode case-folding tables. The file lands in the protected zone (the FS resolves the inode) but the string comparison fails (``ＣＣ/blueprints/x.json``.lower() != ``cc/blueprints/x.json``) so ``startswith`` returns False and the protected-zone check misses. Fix: ``unicodedata.normalize("NFKC", path).casefold()`` for BOTH sides of the prefix comparison. NFKC collapses compatibility variants (fullwidth → ASCII); casefold handles ß → ss and Turkish I. PROTECTED_FILES / PROTECTED_PREFIXES are ASCII by project convention so the normalization is a no-op on the expected-path side, but the defensive normalization closes the bypass class.
documented_in: tests/test_hooks.py::TestUnicodeNormalization (8 tests covering fullwidth tools/, fully-fullwidth, mixed case, uppercase .CLAUDE/, plus ASCII baseline + root + Unicode allowlist non-regression)
